text:
Maria: heads-up — noticed a couple of messy handoffs during last night's PG4 incident. paging timeline was fine, but we lost context during the 02:15 -> 03:00 oncall handoff and customer-impact flags weren't propagated. thinking we should automate the handoff + postmortem kickoff so action items don't fall through.

Ajay: +1. saw the same. we had to re-explain the customer timeline twice. also the severity tag on the ticket didn't get updated to reflect 'partial outage' in Intercom, so CS kept asking for updates. :grimacing:

Lee: quick question — when you say "automate handoff", do you mean a bot that creates the postmortem and assigns owners, or just a templated message?

Maria: both ideally. minimal friction: when an incident is acknowledged and crosses X minutes or has customer-impact label, run: 1) create PM draft in /postmortems backlog, 2) ping next shift with summary, 3) surface action-items in a dashboard. want to reduce manual scheduling.

oncall-bot: Incident Alert: PG4 - Inference cluster CPU spike (ack at 2025-11-12T02:05Z). Paging routed to @oncall. Severity: S2. Customers affected: partial degradation.

Sarah: +1 on dashboard. Right now we use a google sheet that's a mess. If opsbot could create a row with incident metadata (start/end, impacted services, customer tags, preliminary owner) that would be huge.

Tim: I prototyped a tiny slash command last month: `/handoff create --incident 12345 --to @next-oncall --note "kv cache miss spike"` — it posted a thread and pinged the person. can extend to create a postmortem card in linear/gh issues.

Ajay: can we make the trigger threshold configurable? e.g., >30m OR customer_count > 3 OR revenue_impact = true. some incidents don't need full postmortem.

Maria: yes. proposal: incident-bot evaluates ruleset. if rule matches, bot creates postmortem draft using template, assigns a reviewer and owner, and schedules a 30-min follow-up meeting in calendar with the owner + primary oncall + CS rep. meeting request should be optional.

Lee: template idea — we should pre-fill: timeline, immediate mitigation steps, customer impact summary (number of customers + affected regions), who paged, who took primary, and a short 'did we meet SLOs?' checkbox. also a section for 'temporary mitigations' and 'long-term remediations'.

opsbot: idea captured — sample postmortem header created:```
Title: [Draft] PG4 - Inference CPU spike — partial customer impact
Start: 2025-11-12T01:52Z
End: 2025-11-12T02:40Z
Impact: partial degradation (n=18 customers, US-West)
Primary: @oncall
Mitigations: scaled down batch size, drained heavy nodes
Owner(s): TBD
```

Sarah: love that. for visibility we should add a stable permalink to the incident timeline in the postmortem draft (link to traces + k8s events). helps reviewers quickly verify.

Tim: for owner assignment logic: prefer rotation owner (current incident commander) else last responder with 'fix' label. we can have an opt-out flag in the created draft if someone wants to take it later.

Ajay: how do we track action items? important that action items have: owner, due date, priority, status, and a link back to the postmortem. we can push action items into the action-tracker board (not just backlog).

Maria: propose an 'Action Tracker Dashboard' (Grafana? or simple NextJS app) that ingests postmortem drafts and exposes filters: open actions, overdue, owner, service, customer-impact. we'd want an API so CS/PM can subscribe to actions relevant to them.

Lee: implementation notes: 1) incident-bot handles triggers and draft creation via webhook 2) opsbot creates linear/issue and links 3) a lambda syncs actions to dashboard db with basic TTL and webhooks for status changes 4) optional weekly digest for PMs with outstanding high-priority actions.

Maria: example rule snippet for the bot (pseudo):```
if incident.duration > 30m or incident.customer_count > 5 or incident.severity >= S2:
    create_postmortem()
    assign_reviewer(rotation.next())
    create_action_tracker_entry()
```

Sarah: +1 on digest. also want an automated nudge flow: if action due in 48h and status != closed, ping owner in #remediation and email them. keep cc to their manager if overdue > 7d.

Tim: UX thing — when the bot creates a draft, include a tiny checklist at top: [ ] assign owner, [ ] set due dates, [ ] link PR/issue, [ ] set customer notifier. That reduces friction.

Ajay: governance — who decides retention for drafts? some drafts will be ephemeral. maybe drafts older than 90d with no linked actions should auto-archive. also audit logs for who edited what.

Maria: agree. also propose a 'postmortem quick-review' workflow: once draft is created, reviewer has 5 business days to either mark 'no full postmortem needed' or schedule full write-up. if no response, escalate to SRE manager. automates follow-ups.

Lee: rough roadmap itemization? 1) define templates and fields (this week) 2) implement bot triggers + draft creation (2 weeks) 3) integrate with issue tracker + action tracker (3-4 weeks) 4) dashboard + digest (4-6 weeks) 5) audits + retention (6 weeks)

Maria: sounds reasonable. who can own the initial template? I can draft and push a PR to the docs repo today. need a volunteer for the bot integration — @Tim?

Tim: can take bot integration. will start a prototype and share a short demo in #eng-sre next Wed.

Sarah: I'll own the dashboard schema and digest logic. happy to pair with Tim on the webhook contract.

Ajay: I'll write up the rule-engine config and a sample config file for edge cases.

opsbot: created task: "Draft incident handoff/postmortem template" assigned to Maria due 2025-11-19. :white_check_mark:

Maria: thanks all — will post the template PR shortly. if anyone has additional constraints (regulatory retention, legal review), add here or DM me. :pray:
